term: one-way actual-world inclusion of possible necessary-ground edges
definition: If two individuals are necessary from w₀ and an existing one directly supports the other at any admitted world, that very support edge holds in w₀. This is only world-to-actual inclusion; it does not require an actual edge to persist in other worlds.
note: Weakened successor to the stronger bidirectional invariance candidate from #495. A finite model with no actual edge and one possible-world edge witnesses that global union well-foundedness is compatible with the failure of this inclusion principle.
